items.followUp: Define impulse and state its relationship to change in momentum.

rubric.why: Awards credit for defining momentum as the product of mass and velocity.
rubric.description: Defines momentum and gives its formula.
rubric.how: State that momentum is the product of an object's mass and velocity, p = mv.

rubric.why: Awards credit for stating that total momentum is unchanged in an isolated system.
rubric.description: States the law of conservation of momentum.
rubric.how: Explain that the total momentum of an isolated system before an interaction equals its total momentum afterwards.

modelAnswer: Momentum is the product of the mass of a body and its velocity: p = mv.
Momentum is a vector quantity and has the direction of the velocity.
The law of conservation of momentum states that the total momentum of an isolated system remains constant.
Thus, total momentum before an interaction equals total momentum after it.

items.followUp: A 2 kg trolley moving at 3 m s⁻¹ collides with a stationary 1 kg trolley. If they move together after collision, find their common velocity.

rubric.why: Awards credit for identifying the given values.
rubric.description: Lists the initial velocity, acceleration and time.
rubric.how: Write u = 4 m s⁻¹, a = 1 m s⁻² and t = 10 s.

rubric.why: Awards credit for selecting the constant-acceleration displacement formula.
rubric.description: Writes the displacement formula.
rubric.how: Use s = ut + ½at².

rubric.why: Awards credit for substituting the given values correctly with units.
rubric.description: Substitutes the values into the formula.
rubric.how: Substitute u = 4 m s⁻¹, a = 1 m s⁻² and t = 10 s.

rubric.why: Awards credit for correctly evaluating the displacement.
rubric.description: Calculates the displacement.
rubric.how: Evaluate 4 × 10 + ½ × 1 × 10² = 90.

rubric.why: Awards credit for giving the final distance with the correct unit.
rubric.description: States the final distance moved.
rubric.how: Give the distance as 90 m.

modelAnswer: Given: u = 4 m s⁻¹, a = 1 m s⁻², t = 10 s.
Formula: s = ut + ½at².
Substitution: s = (4 m s⁻¹)(10 s) + ½(1 m s⁻²)(10 s)².
Calculation: s = 40 m + 50 m = 90 m.
Answer: The bicycle moves 90 m.

items.followUp: Describe the energy changes that take place when a stretched bow launches an arrow.

rubric.why: Awards credit for explaining that interconversion means energy changes from one form into another.
rubric.description: Explains interconversion of energy.
rubric.how: State that energy can change from one form to another.

rubric.why: Awards credit for a suitable example and identifying the energy forms involved.
rubric.description: Gives and explains an example of energy interconversion.
rubric.how: For example, as a body falls, its gravitational potential energy changes into kinetic energy.

modelAnswer: Interconversion of energy is the change of energy from one form into another.
For example, a raised body has gravitational potential energy.
As the body falls, its potential energy decreases and its kinetic energy increases.
Thus, gravitational potential energy is converted into kinetic energy.

items.followUp: A room measures 6 m × 4 m × 3 m. Find the mass of air in it if the density of air is 1.2 kg m⁻³.

rubric.why: Awards credit for finding the room's volume.
rubric.description: Calculates the volume of the room.
rubric.how: Use V = 8 m × 5 m × 4 m = 160 m³.

rubric.why: Awards credit for identifying the density of air.
rubric.description: Records the given density.
rubric.how: Write ρ = 1.3 kg m⁻³.

rubric.why: Awards credit for choosing the relationship between mass, density and volume.
rubric.description: Writes the mass formula.
rubric.how: Use m = ρV.

rubric.why: Awards credit for correct substitution.
rubric.description: Substitutes the density and volume.
rubric.how: Substitute m = (1.3 kg m⁻³)(160 m³).

rubric.why: Awards credit for the correct mass and unit.
rubric.description: States the final mass of air.
rubric.how: Give the mass as 208 kg.

modelAnswer: Given: ρ = 1.3 kg m⁻³; room dimensions are 8 m × 5 m × 4 m.
Volume: V = 8 m × 5 m × 4 m = 160 m³.
Formula: m = ρV.
Substitution: m = (1.3 kg m⁻³)(160 m³) = 208 kg.
Answer: The mass of air in the room is 208 kg.

items.followUp: Define oscillatory motion and give one example other than a vibrating tuning fork.

rubric.why: Awards credit for defining vibratory motion as repeated to-and-fro motion about a mean position.
rubric.description: Defines vibratory motion.
rubric.how: State that it is a repeated to-and-fro motion about a mean position.

rubric.why: Awards credit for giving a suitable example.
rubric.description: Gives an example of vibratory motion.
rubric.how: For example, the oscillation of a pendulum.

modelAnswer: Vibratory motion is the repeated to-and-fro motion of a body about its mean position.
The oscillation of a pendulum is an example.

items.followUp: Convert 90 km h⁻¹ into m s⁻¹.

rubric.why: Awards credit for using the correct conversion factors from kilometres per hour to metres per second.
rubric.description: Shows the unit conversion.
rubric.how: Use 1 km = 1000 m and 1 h = 3600 s.

rubric.why: Awards credit for calculating the speed in SI units.
rubric.description: Gives the speed in metres per second.

modelAnswer: Given speed = 200 km h⁻¹.
Conversion: 1 km = 1000 m and 1 h = 3600 s.
Speed in SI units = 200 × 1000 ÷ 3600 m s⁻¹.
Answer: The speed is 55.56 m s⁻¹ (approximately).

items.followUp: Find the acceleration produced by a 15 N force acting on a 5 kg mass.

rubric.why: Awards credit for using Newton's second law to find acceleration.
rubric.description: Writes the acceleration formula.
rubric.how: Use a = F/m.

rubric.why: Awards credit for substituting the values and giving the correct SI answer.
rubric.description: Calculates and states the acceleration.
rubric.how: Calculate a = 20 N ÷ 8 kg = 2.5 m s⁻².

modelAnswer: Given: F = 20 N, m = 8 kg.
Formula: a = F/m.
Substitution: a = 20 N ÷ 8 kg = 2.5 m s⁻².
Answer: The acceleration is 2.5 m s⁻².

items.followUp: State the two conditions for equilibrium of a rigid body.

rubric.why: Awards credit for stating the first condition for equilibrium.
rubric.description: States the first condition for equilibrium.
rubric.how: The resultant force on the body must be zero.

rubric.why: Awards credit for stating the second condition for equilibrium.
rubric.description: States the second condition for equilibrium.
rubric.how: The resultant torque about any point must be zero.

modelAnswer: First condition: The resultant force acting on a body must be zero (ΣF = 0).
Second condition: The resultant torque acting on a body about any point must be zero (Στ = 0).
